title: Knowledge check: Saving, Updating, and Deleting Records

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed for “Saving, Updating, and Deleting Records”?
options: A complete substitute for server-side validation
A guarantee that every database write succeeds atomically
A feature that is always enabled without configuration
questions.explanation: The supplied Django curriculum lists “Creating model instances” under lesson 64, “Saving, Updating, and Deleting Records”. The lesson connects this item to the practical Django workflow for django models and database fundamentals.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports reliable work on “Saving, Updating, and Deleting Records”?
options: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
Assume the browser is trusted and skip server-side checks.
Copy a production secret into the source file so every environment matches.
Publish an example before checking framework/version compatibility.
questions.answer_key: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
questions.explanation: Small reproducible examples, server-side validation where relevant, and explicit positive/negative checks help distinguish expected behavior from assumptions. Version, environment, and boundary cases should be documented.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most appropriate when applying “Saving, Updating, and Deleting Records” in a real application?
options: Add indexes to every field without checking query plans.
Materialize every database row into memory before filtering.
Assume that reducing query count always makes every request faster.
Measure query behavior and verify the proposed optimization with representative data.
questions.answer_key: Measure query behavior and verify the proposed optimization with representative data.
questions.explanation: The lesson is part of Django Models and Database Fundamentals. Select the approach that supports correctness, safe handling of failures, and verifiable behavior; see the linked official documentation for version-specific details.

notes: Answer keys and explanations remain in the server-side course repository. The existing CodeLeaf GET handler strips answers until grading; this course does not expose solutions in public lesson content.
